proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the global two-plane cancellation factorization and a fixed-compact Gaussian-tail transfer, then used them to close the split-role Gaussian frontier, bounded-count product-Poisson transition, and conservative rational confidence construction. A bounded validity repair made all limit and sampling premises explicit, replaced the underspecified CLT citation with a self-contained proof, exposed the observed-law functional, and left all 15 graph statements proved. The result remains incremental because the motivating reused-block panel is not covered; a field-tier advance would require a new overlapping-block sampling and covariance architecture.
tldr: For every probability triple in the open unit cube, the normal-link and multiplicative distributional-DiD maps agree exactly on the two planes \(p_1=p_3\) or \(p_2=p_3\), and their complete off-plane discrepancy has a cancellation-safe signed-rectangle factorization. On the comparable-rarity box, the resolved common-cutoff theorem sharpens its coefficient uniformly to \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\), including both planes. The resulting Gaussian drift frontiers, bounded-count product-Poisson limits, and finitely terminating rational confidence intervals are proved for the deliberately independent sixty-role split design.
gap: The normal-link DTT identity is Djuazon and Tsyawo's published baseline. Their Assumption 5 requires a fixed positive lower bound on \(\phi(\Phi^{-1}(F_{gt}(y)))\), which is impossible on comparable-rarity arrays because \(\phi(q(\rho_n c_{\ell j,n}))\to0\). One-dimensional Mills bounds, Gaussian second-order delta methods, and generic multinomial inversion do not settle the mixed cancellation coefficient or its two exact planes.
fill: The project derives the exact factorization first, isolates the common-cutoff uniform bound as the open analytic kernel, and carries it through Gaussian and product-Poisson limits and certified finite-sample outer inference.
